### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94fb8db2d170543fbd770f89849164d4b51e2e48` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dab3ecb504173e45649a87bc8013a117536b8ae1` — the merge of head `692d874e9376e11616cfdfd0502865db774e9101` into base `94fb8db2d170543fbd770f89849164d4b51e2e48`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dab3ecb504173e45649a87bc8013a117536b8ae1 && git checkout dab3ecb504173e45649a87bc8013a117536b8ae1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 94fb8db2d170543fbd770f89849164d4b51e2e48 692d874e9376e11616cfdfd0502865db774e9101 && git checkout -B drift-repro 94fb8db2d170543fbd770f89849164d4b51e2e48 && git merge --no-ff 692d874e9376e11616cfdfd0502865db774e9101

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94fb8db2d170543fbd770f89849164d4b51e2e48
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：保存配置被拒时，错误列表里不再先出现一句空洞的"输入无效"，第一条就是真正出错的位置和原因；自带说明的那类提示照常保留。
- 为什么做：按你的裁决"每层都去掉，表单另立单"，那句空话不指出任何字段，只会挡在真正原因前面。
- 出错会怎样：按位置读第一条错误的程序会读到不同内容；设计器里约 25 个字段在保存被拒后暂时少一行红字，等表单那张单落地后恢复。
- 要你做什么：无。区域合并主线后，席位做合同复审，再由区域落地。
- 席位意见：实现与你的裁决一致；落地前须先合并主线，另请席位复核"收窄"声明的写法。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT** · head `62387026dbfc4810b024d27774b340599ed427a0` · Fixes #35400 (scope ruling 7008570921) · 2026-11-19T14:13Z · reviewed to `pm-dispatch` text at `origin/main` `fca72dfa32`

Readings: `check-governed-merges --pr 35520` not governed; `merge-tree` against main clean; CI 37 success / 16 skipped / 0 failed. **K=15**: merge main and get a green re-run before queueing. A merge-only push needs no fresh L1. The dogfood battery is on this head (7011518520: 482 files / 4092 tests, 0 failures), as `l1-review-checklist.md` asks of a `!` / `(narrowing)` PR. Mark the draft ready after the merge.

**Code (`protocol-metadata-issues.ts`), read in full on the head.** In `collectMetadataIssues`:
- A non-expandable issue is deduped and pushed, and the function returns, as before.
- A union collects its branches' entries into `below`, then pushes the head only if `below` is empty or its message is not `ZOD_UNION_DEFAULT_MESSAGE` (`'Invalid input'`), then pushes `below`. So an explained bare head is dropped at every depth, while a head carrying the schema's own sentence, or one nothing explains, is kept ahead of its causes.
- Container heads are pushed first, unchanged.
- The constant is exported only for its pin, not re-exported from `protocol.ts`.

This is exactly the ruling's first bullet. The texts the ruling named as becoming false are corrected in this PR: the `collectMetadataIssues` and `zodIssuesToMetadataIssues` docblocks, and `metadata-diagnostics.ts:333-335`.

**Pins.**
- A real-zod PIN of the default text.
- Bare-and-explained is dropped, while the same tree with its own sentence keeps the head.
- A view's `label: {not_a_locale}` gives only the `label.not_a_locale` entries.
- `titleFormat` and `confirmText` written as formulas keep their authored heads.
- CONTROL: `label: 42` keeps its bare head.
- Parity §4 records that the terminal (`formatZodError`) and the data API (`zodIssuesToFields`) keep the head.

The 23 removed `expect` lines are the old head-first pins (`issues[0]` is `invalid_union`, `length > 1`, path lists starting with `''`), each replaced by the new order. None is a weakened rejection: `code` and the 422 face are still asserted.

**Changeset: sentences checked against the diff.** The Was / Now table matches the label and view cases pinned above and the `meta-envelope` headline change. The "What stays" list, union heads that carry the schema's own sentence, unexplained heads and container entries, matches the three keep branches. "Unchanged, on purpose" (CLI and data API) matches parity §4. The known Studio-form regression is the ruling's own consequence line, and #35499 tracks it. The text also carries the BREAKING banner, the migration (read by `path` / `code`) and one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which the gate in Check Changeset accepted on this head. `Skills-docs: none` is in the PR body, with its search stated.

**Declaration: one point for the seat's L2.** The PR and the ruling record both spell `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:113-116` reads `yes (narrowing)` as a diff that widens one surface and narrows another, and `no (narrowing)` as a pure narrowing. I find no surface this diff widens. If the seat agrees, the spelling should be `no (narrowing)`, the #35444 precedent. Because the ruling record names the current spelling, I leave the call to the seat that recorded it rather than making it an R item. `Metadata-protocol: none` and patch are right either way.

**Routing.** L2 is owed for the narrowing declaration at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` by seat 5, on the merged head. ux-3 lands after it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `692d874e9376e11616cfdfd0502865db774e9101`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-metadata-issues.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.save-union-issues.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/union-branch-policy.cross-package-parity.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.union-issues.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.container-issue-descent.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.invalid-metadata-422-face-inventory.test.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-client-failures.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/package.json, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/zod-issues-to-fields.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/error-map.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action-copy-template.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/pm/label-write.mjs

Judged against card #35400: the first ruling (comment 7003683081, drop the head when an entry below explains it) as refined by the scope ruling (comment 7008570921: every depth, only zod's bare `Invalid input`, an authored sentence stays, an unexplained head stays, container heads unchanged, a pin on zod's text, the form side to its own card #35499, the false in-repo texts moved in the same PR). Net diff read against `main` `94fb8db2d1`, which is the head's merge-base: 8 files, +360 / -88. Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 39 success, 18 skipped by their own filter, 0 failed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of every metadata type: unchanged. Right.** The producer runs only after a `safeParse` has already failed at each of its four call sites (`protocol-save.ts:1570-1572`, `metadata-diagnostics.ts:312-338`, `protocol-client-failures.ts:675-676`, `protocol-package-commits.ts:662-664`). No schema file is in the diff; which bodies are refused, and with which status and code, does not move. `Metadata-protocol: none` follows.
- **Membership of a published refusal list: narrowed. Right, and declared.** `issues[]` of `422 INVALID_METADATA`, `_diagnostics.errors` on reads, the seed-request refusal and the unmanaged-import `400` share the one producer, so all four lose a union's own entry when it is bare and explained. Element shape `{ path, message, code }` is untouched. An entry removed from a published response is breaking for a positional reader; the title's `!`, the BREAKING banner and the `(narrowing)` arm say so.
- **Sentences rendered from the list move with it. Right.** `metadataIssueHeadline` (count plus the first three locators, `protocol-client-failures.ts:704-709`), the message-only face's first-three slice (`protocol-write-face.ts:96-99`) and the boot warning's first entry (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts:1348`) now spend their slots on located causes. These are human-read strings on faces that carry the same findings structurally or carry none; no reader in `packages/` or `ui/` selects a served entry by `invalid_union` or by `slice(1`.
- **Public surface: not widened. Right.** `ZOD_UNION_DEFAULT_MESSAGE` (`protocol-metadata-issues.ts:63`) is a module-level export only: `protocol.ts:434-435` re-exports `zodIssuesToMetadataIssues` and `MetadataIssueEntry` and nothing else from that module, and the package's `exports` map addresses `.` alone, so the constant is not reachable from the published entry.
- **The other two walks: unchanged. Right.** `zodIssuesToFields` still pushes every head (`packages/spec/src/api/zod-issues-to-fields.ts:214`) and `formatZodIssue` still prints it as the parent line; neither file is in the diff. The asymmetry is asserted, not normalised away (parity test §4, line 484).

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch` is the right level: the kind is `none`, the only package whose source the diff moves is that one, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right line, line-initial on both carriers (PR body line 8, changeset body). The value answers whether the card widens an accept set or enlarges a public surface: it does neither (① above). `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:113-116` gives `no (narrowing)` as "not a widening, but breaking" and reserves `yes (narrowing)` for a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. The two ruling comments and both claim lines on the card spell `yes (narrowing)`; that is the seat's transcription under "as executed", not the maintainer's quoted words, which rule scope only. The head's spelling is the truthful one and costs nothing the ruling asked for: banner, was/now table, the reading instruction, exactly one ADR-0087 marker and the dogfood arm are all present or triggered either way.
- The changeset carries both declaration lines, the BREAKING banner, a was/now table whose first two rows match the pins in `protocol.save-union-issues.test.ts` (the repro fixture at line 139; the `label` map case), the instruction to read by `path` and `code`, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker whose reason holds (nothing authorable moves and nothing is stored: `_diagnostics` is recomputed per read behind an in-memory memo keyed by content), what stays, the two unchanged walks with #35433, and the known Studio regression with #35499. Both `Check Changeset` runs and every lint lane are green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round-1 open question (which scope ships) is answered by the scope ruling 7008570921. The final report (comment 7011455182) carries no open question.
- Dev deviations, each answered: (1) draft opened after local verification: no contract effect. (2) the PR is still a draft: flipping it is a landing step, below. (3) four pin files import `./lint-root-preload.testkit.js` at module top: the testkit exists in the package and the import is inside the claimed test files; accepted. (4) commit trailers are the model-free pair: accepted. (5) no `ui/` path and no `zod-issues-to-fields.ts` change: confirmed on the file list.
- Out-of-scope findings: #35433 (open) and #35499 (open) carry the first two. The third has no carrier: the Save tooltip's leading comma can remain when a view's root head keeps its own sentence. It is a read-only inference under `ui/`; the seat attaches it to #35499 or files it through the filing gate. Escalated, not blocking.
- The card's claim lines (7004194733, 7008644070) still read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` while both gate-read carriers read `no (narrowing)`. No gate reads the claim; the seat may amend it for the record.
- **Landing prerequisites, none met by this record.** (a) The land gate's dogfood leg will refuse this head as it stands: the newest `os-dev-report` on #35400 (7011455182) pins the battery at `62387026db`, and the head's own commit `692d874e93` sits above it with one parent, so the first-parent walk stops there (`scripts/pm/label-write.mjs`, `landDogfoodGate`: only two-parent merges of the base are stepped over). A new report whose `dogfood_battery` opens with this head, or with a sha this head reaches through merges of the base alone, is owed first. The commit in question changes one changeset line; the gate has no prose exemption. (b) The PR is a draft. (c) The PR body's Tests and Verification sections name `62387026db` as the final head; the readings there predate the merge of `main` `94fb8db2d1`.
- PR author is the fleet relay; no outside-author note is owed.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to find.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** The spec declares the list once, as `MetadataValidationResultSchema.errors`: an optional array of `{ path, message, code? }` whose `path` is described as the path to the invalid field (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:538-542`). It declares no entry for a union as such, no order and no index. The entry this PR removes named no invalid field of its own (path `''`, or a slot the entries under it name more exactly) and carried zod's default text, so nothing the spec declares is taken away at the consumer; the list moves toward what the spec describes. What IS reversed is a released promise in prose (the 17.0.0 changelog's "strictly additive, `issues[0]` unmoved"), and that reversal is the maintainer's, twice ruled, and declared as breaking. This is not a capability narrowed at the consumer in place of an implementation gap.

**The rule, read in the code** (`protocol-metadata-issues.ts:292-303`). The expansion collects into a local `below`, then pushes the head unless `below` is non-empty and the head's message equals the constant. Checked against the ruling limb by limb:

- every depth: the test is inside the recursive walk, no depth or path condition. Holds.
- only the bare text: exact string equality with `ZOD_UNION_DEFAULT_MESSAGE`. A union declared with its own `error` keeps its head: the typed-slot sentences (`packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts`), an action's copy-slot sentence (`packages/spec/src/ui/action-copy-template.ts:160`) and a view union's retirement prescription (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`) are such heads. Three pins hold the split: one synthetic tree with both messages, an object `titleFormat` and an action `confirmText`. No global zod locale or error map is configured in `packages/` or `ui/`, and the three parses read here pass no per-parse map, so the call sites see the default text the pin parses.
- an unexplained head stays: with nothing selected `below` is empty (pinned by `label: 42`, line 511); zod's empty `errors` and the depth bound never enter the branch at all (`:284-290`), so they are untouched.
- container heads unchanged: `:306-310` pushes the head unconditionally. Pinned in two files.
- the pin on zod's text: `protocol.save-union-issues.test.ts:426`, through a plain `z.union` and through the real view schema.
- the texts that became false: the entry-rule docblock, the `zodIssuesToMetadataIssues` docblock and `metadata-diagnostics.ts:333-337` now state the rule the code runs. The remaining "additive" sentences in the package are about the container descent, which is still additive.

**Tried to break it.**

- Ordering and de-duplication: apart from the drop, the walk is the one on `main`. The leaf path, the `seen` key and the exemption of expanded heads are unchanged, and a kept head still precedes its causes.
- A chain of bare heads to the depth bound collapses to the deepest one alone (pinned). No location is lost: each dropped head sat at a prefix of the kept one's path.
- A union whose only explanation is a nested bare head at the same slot leaves exactly one such entry. Equivalent to what the outer head said.
- A discriminator miss (`errors: []`, bare text) is not expandable and stays. Correct: it is the whole answer.
- Non-union issues whose text happens to be `Invalid input` are never candidates; only the union branch drops.
- §2 of the parity test now compares this envelope with the two spec walks after projecting out explained bare heads (`withoutExplainedBareHeads`, line 188), and compares the two spec walks with each other head for head, so branch selection is still one verdict in three places. The projection is positional (bare text, next pair at or under the slot) rather than the producer's rule; it is exact on the seven fixtures and it is test scaffolding, so it is noted and not graded.

**Per file.** `protocol-metadata-issues.ts`: implements the ruling as read above. `metadata-diagnostics.ts`: comment only, now true. `protocol.save-union-issues.test.ts`: the moved pins assert the absence of the root head and the located cause at index 0; the new block pins the constant, both sides of the bare/authored split on one tree, and three real-schema cases plus the unexplained control. `union-branch-policy.cross-package-parity.test.ts`: records the asymmetry and keeps the unexplained-head control across all three walks. The other three test files move only the assertions the drop moved.

**Findings.**

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — `protocol-metadata-issues.ts:301`, with the docblock at `:219-221`. "Explained" is decided by `below.length`, and `below` only receives entries `seen` has not already let through. When two tied branches of an outer union each fail on the same nested bare union with the same leaf cause, the second nested head finds every one of its entries de-duplicated, reads as unexplained and is kept, after its cause: the list ends `[cause at x, bare head at x]`. The docblock's list of unexplained cases (bare kind mismatch, empty `errors`, depth bound) does not name this one, and there the head is not "the whole answer". Reasoned from the code; not measured on a real schema (read-only round), and it cannot touch a top-level head, since `seen` is fresh per top-level issue. It is no regression (the same input on `main` carried that head and one more) and it contradicts neither the ruling's wording nor the changeset's ("an entry below it explains"). A fix would decide "explained" from the selection being non-empty; that moves code, so it belongs on a follow-up card, or stands as an accepted deviation. Not to be fixed on this head.

**VERDICT: PASS**
